title: Cut total batch size 4x (2^19 -> 2^17)
description: TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**19 -> 2**17 and DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128 -> 64 (grad_accum 1); nothing else changed.
reflection: Neutral-to-slightly-worse: val_bpb 0.997662 vs baseline 0.997359 (+0.0003). My premise was simply wrong: throughput is ~1.3M tok/s, so the baseline was never step-starved -- it ran ~780 steps / ~409M tokens, not ~300 steps. At 2^17 I got 3119 steps and the identical 408.8M tokens (MFU 32.8%, peak VRAM 22.7GB, down from the baseline's larger footprint). So a 4x batch change at fixed LR moves val_bpb by <0.0004: this setup sits on a flat plateau across 128K-512K tokens/step, and the implied 4x change in effective LR per token did not hurt either, which says the LR is not near an edge. Two things follow for the group: (1) the batch-size axis is spent, do not buy another run on it; (2) the Muon momentum ramp (get_muon_momentum, 300 steps) finishes in the first ~10-40% of training in every configuration, so it is not the lever I speculated it might be. Remaining gains have to come from architecture, model size, or the data/token budget, not from the optimizer step count.
